nbg_001: You can recognise it by its gnarled, storm-damaged trunk, still putting on growth, at the southern end of the meadow. It stands in Hallerwiese park, two large planes on the green behind it.
nbg_003: You can recognise it as one of a pair of large planes about forty metres apart, on the green just behind the gnarled lime. It stands in Hallerwiese park.
nbg_004: You can recognise it in May by hundreds of white flower candles standing upright over the crown, and later by spiny conker cases. It stands in Kontumazgarten, near the playground.
nbg_005: You can recognise it as one of three planes among six individually protected trees packed within about 150 metres of each other. It stands in Kontumazgarten.
nbg_006: You can recognise it by the bare ground beneath its dense canopy and its smooth grey bark, which shows every old scar. It stands in Kontumazgarten, one of two protected beeches there.
nbg_009: You can recognise it by turning copper and holding the colour through late autumn, the last of the park's six protected trees. It stands in Kontumazgarten.
nbg_010: You can recognise it by its trunk, about 8 metres round, one of the strongest and oldest in the city. It stands in the Stadtpark, south of the Schiller monument.
nbg_011: You can recognise it as one of two separately registered beeches standing about eighty metres apart. It stands in Cramer-Klett-Park, Gärten bei Wöhrd.
nbg_012: You can recognise it as the other of the two separately registered beeches, about eighty metres from its neighbour. It stands in Cramer-Klett-Park, Gärten bei Wöhrd.
